panoramica.options.keybind.desc: The key or mouse button used to take a panorama screenshot.
panoramica.options.keybind.duplicate_des:
This key is also used for:
%s
panoramica.options.resolution.low_256.de: Lowest resolution. Fast to capture and very small on disk, but noticeably softer than Minecraft's modern menu backgrounds.
panoramica.options.resolution.balanced_5: A lightweight middle option. Sharper than 256x256 while still keeping captures quick and files modest.
panoramica.options.resolution.default_10: Recommended default. Matches the size used by modern Minecraft menu panoramas and gives a clean background without being excessive.
panoramica.options.resolution.very_high_: Higher than the normal menu background size. Useful for very large displays, with larger files and a longer capture pause.
panoramica.options.resolution.ultra_2048: Maximum preset. Best when you want extra-sharp panorama files, but it uses the most memory, disk space, and capture time.
panoramica.options.menu_mode.desc: Chooses which panorama is used behind menu screens. If no matching panorama is available, Minecraft's vanilla panorama is shown.
panoramica.options.menu_parallax.desc: Gently tilts and turns the menu background panorama toward the mouse cursor.
panoramica.options.cycle_interval.desc: How long each panorama stays visible when the menu background mode cycles through multiple panoramas.
panoramica.options.cycle_interval.inacti: Only used when "Menu Background" is set to a mode that can cycle through multiple panoramas.
panoramica.options.storage.desc: Chooses the parent folder for new panorama screenshots. Each capture is still saved in its own timestamped subfolder.
panoramica.options.hide_hud_normal_scree: Hides the in-game HUD before saving normal Minecraft screenshots. This only affects normal screenshots; panorama screenshots always hide the HUD. Menus and other open screens are not hidden.
panoramica.options.preview_mode.desc: Chooses which screenshot types show a small preview in the top-left corner for 10 seconds after capture.
panoramica.options.screenshot_chat_messa: Shows or hides chat messages from normal and panorama screenshots. Screenshots are still saved either way.
panoramica.options.screenshot_buttons_vi: When disabled, it hides Panoramica's screenshot browser icon buttons from the title screen and pause screen.

After hiding these screenshot buttons, the only way to access Panoramica's options
is through NeoForge's Mods menu. On Fabric, use Mod Menu's Mods menu instead.

panoramica.photo_mode.title: Photo Mode
panoramica.photo_mode.unavailable: Photo mode can only be used while in a world.
panoramica.photo_mode.pause.desc: Pauses or unpauses the integrated singleplayer game while photo mode stays usable.
panoramica.photo_mode.pause.unavailable_: Photo mode pausing is unavailable because you are on a server.
panoramica.photo_mode.grid.desc: Shows a translucent rule-of-thirds grid over the photo view.
panoramica.photo_mode.vignette.desc: Darkens the edges of the view so the center draws more attention. Keep it low for a subtle camera feel, or raise it for a stronger cinematic frame.
panoramica.photo_mode.depth_of_field.des: Turns on a camera-style blur that keeps your chosen focus area sharp while nearer or farther parts of the scene soften. Great for portraits, close-ups, and cinematic shots.
panoramica.photo_mode.dof_focus_distance: Sets how far from the camera the sharpest point should be. Move it until your subject is clear; objects much nearer or farther away will blur.
panoramica.photo_mode.dof_focal_length.d: Changes how strongly the lens separates your subject from the background. Higher values make the focused area feel tighter and the blur more dramatic.
panoramica.photo_mode.dof_aperture.desc: Controls how wide the virtual lens opens. Lower numbers create stronger blur and softer backgrounds; higher numbers keep more of the scene clear.
panoramica.photo_mode.saturation.desc: Controls how intense the colors feel. Lower values fade the image toward gray; higher values make colors richer and livelier.
panoramica.photo_mode.contrast.desc: Controls the separation between dark and bright areas. Lower values soften the image; higher values add punch and shape, but can hide some shadow detail.
panoramica.photo_mode.overexposure.desc: Controls how strongly light is pushed across the image. Raise it for brighter, glowing highlights; lower it for a darker, more restrained look.
panoramica.photo_mode.colorize.desc: Applies a finished color preset over the photo view. Use it to quickly change the mood, then fine-tune the result with the other Effects sliders.
panoramica.photo_mode.pose.desc: Select a pose for your player.
panoramica.photo_mode.pose_maker.title: Pose Maker
panoramica.photo_mode.time.desc: Changes the rendered sky and lighting without changing the world's real time.
panoramica.photo_mode.weather.desc: Changes rendered weather without changing the world's real weather.
panoramica.photo_mode.return_to_player.d: Moves the photo camera back to its player-facing starting position without changing photo settings.
panoramica.photo_mode.hide_gui.desc: Hide the photo mode interface. Press H to bring it back.
panoramica.photo_mode.confirm.hide_gui.m: This will hide the full photo mode interface. Press H to bring it back.
panoramica.photo_mode.confirm.reset.mess: This will restore all settings to their defaults.
panoramica.photo_mode.confirm.leave.mess: Close photo mode and return to normal gameplay.
panoramica.photo_mode.screenshot.unavail: Photo mode screenshots can only be taken while in a world.
